Logan / Karthik — I ran an ops-level sizing + risk scan based on Erin’s numbers. Summary below (short answer: we can support a soft hold and recommend a conservative node plan).

Sizing assumptions (from Crescent):
- 18M tokens/day sustained (~540M tokens/month)
- Model: ~80B architecture; quantized path available (4-bit)
- Peak concurrency: 220 qps (bursts)

Baseline recommendation (production-ready cluster):
- Node type: 8x H100 (pod-equivalent use) or 8x A100-80GB depending on availability
- Recommended fleet count: 10 nodes (H100) / 14 nodes (A100) to meet sustained throughput + 25% buffer for bursts and pre-warm KV cache
- Estimated aggregate throughput: ~260 qps sustained (H100 cluster) with ~90ms p50 for 512-token contexts; A100 cluster: ~210 qps sustained p50 ~120ms
- Token cost delta: H100 baseline ~18% lower per-token at this sizing once sustained batching is applied (rough estimate)

Soft-hold policy suggestion:
- Place a soft, non-billable hold on the 10-node H100-equivalent capacity for 28 days. During the soft-hold we do not provision fully but mark capacity in our scheduler and avoid allocation to flexible pools.
- If Crescent moves to a committed reservation (signed SOW + PO) within 28 days, we convert to a firm allocation and schedule provisioning (2–3 week lead for guaranteed nodes).
- If no conversion after 28 days, we release hold automatically.

Risks / mitigations:
- Fleet tightness in Q4 could reduce the ability to convert H100 holds to firm allocations without a commercial commit; fallback is to provision A100 cluster with dynamic autoscale and a mix of quantized model variants.
- Recommend Crescent confirm willingness to test 4-bit quantized variant in pilot to reduce node count.

Attachments:
- [attachment: capacity-plan-crescent-20290910.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45 KB)]

I’ll also create a short ops note with node-level IO and pre-warm instructions if we convert to firm. Logging this as a requested soft-hold in our internal runway tracker (hubspot link below).
